title: Why do I have Anal Pain?
description: Does it hurt for you to sit down for long periods of time, or when using the restroom? These could be signs of a bigger problem. ---- Dr. Lynn O'Connor, MD MPH FACS FASCRS, is a highly respected colorectal surgeon. Her mission is to provide her patients with the foremost treatment, technology and information related to preventive public health issues and colon and rectal health. She is outspoken about declining health patterns due to lack of exercise, growing obesity and the increase in colon cancer among the U.S. population.  Dr. O'Connor is the director of Colon and Rectal Surgery of New York.   She is a sought after speaker, lecturing nationally on advanced techniques related to colorectal therapeutic considerations. She has not only excelled in academia, but garnered many honors and awards throughout the years, making her an influential leader in colorectal medicine.  Dr. O'Connor's education includes:  Colon & Rectal Fellowship, Georgia Colon & Rectal Surgical Clinic Atlanta, GA General Surgery Residency, Union Memorial Hospital Baltimore, MD  Radiation Oncology Fellowship, Johns Hopkins Hospital, Baltimore, MD  MD, Temple University School of Medicine Philadelphia, PA  MPH, Yale University, New Haven, CT  B.S. Biology, Rutgers University, New Brunswick, NJ  https://www.colonandrectalsurgeryofnewyork.com/  Find her on Facebook here: https://www.facebook.com/lynnoconnormd Find her on Twitter here: https://twitter.com/lynnoconnormd https://bizyellow.com/businesses/colon-and-rectal-surgery-new-york

asr.full_text: Something my patients frequently call and complain about is anal pain, and it's pain after going to the bathroom, it's pain sometimes from prolonged sitting. And they have anal pain and they're not really sure. Anal pain can be due to several factors such as hemorrhoids, fissures, fistula, and even an abscess. Sometimes a cancer may cause anal pain. So if you are experiencing anal pain, and especially if youcess. Sometimes a cancer may cause anal pain, so if you are experiencing anal pain and especially if you're experiencing anal pain with other symptoms such as change in bowel habits, rectal bleeding, you need to come in for a consultation. So if there's something that's different, something that's a little off that you're not sure of and this pain is persistent, you need to come in for a consultation. I'd be more than happy to help you and take care of you.
